appStatus: builds and runs (Next.js 14, 21 routes); tests 7/7; PDF report generated (11pp)
keyFindings: Official multi-agency data review underway (OC HCA + CA Cancer Registry + UCI + OC Ag Commissioner); no cluster or cause declared. Findings still pending as of 2026-07-18; no EPA response to the federal request.

PUR EMPIRICAL FINDING: 94.6% of Orange County pesticide records have no location; landscape maintenance is 15,383 records but only 0.1% geolocated. Ladera Ranch sits in unsectioned PLSS land (T7S R7W/R8W, section=00). PUR is structurally incapable of placing an application inside Ladera Ranch.

CORRECTED GEOMETRY: two plugged/abandoned oil & gas wells lie within ~1 mile of the community centroid (0.25 mi and 0.77 mi), not 2.0-2.7 mi as first recorded. Places the community inside the exposure contrast of the 2026 abandoned-well/Ewing study. Raises priority; does not establish exposure.

TIMING: the 'toxic soil' hypothesis splits into two mechanisms with opposite birth-cohort predictions. Construction-era dust (1999-2006) is substantially weakened for recent diagnoses (93% of ages overlap grading for a 2013 dx, only 7% for 2026) and unavailable for children born after ~2007. Persistent soil residue (arsenic never degrades) is UNAFFECTED by timing. Birth year is the discriminating test and is the missing data.

ARSENIC REVISED DOWN to low-prior: SoCal background (12 mg/kg upper bound) swamps risk-based screening levels (0.11-0.68); measured bioavailability ~0.31 at the closest analogue; lead arsenate was an apple/pear insecticide not citrus; mass grading likely diluted; null biomarker correlation at comparable soil levels; systematic review finds no arsenic-childhood-cancer association. Not excluded, never measured here, but no longer the leading environmental explanation.

SCREENING MODEL now separates exposure opportunity from disease-specific plausibility. Glufosinate drops #2->#5; abandoned oil/gas wells rise to #1 as the only candidate with a disease-matched published signal.

PUR independently confirms glufosinate as a major regional landscape herbicide (442 records, 10,531.9 lbs OC 2023; 336 in landscape maintenance) - ordinary regional practice, not evidence of causation. Glyphosate is larger.
All pesticide-specific causal claims remain advocacy/attorney-sourced (grade C); glufosinate is not classified a carcinogen by any regulator (EU non-renewal was on reproductive toxicity).
Ewing sarcoma is ancestry-driven (~9x higher in European ancestry); this 63.6% non-Hispanic-white community has an elevated baseline expectation.
Strongest testable environmental lead: legacy agricultural soil residue on former farmland (confirmed at neighboring DTSC school sites, never tested on the footprint).
Drinking water low-plausibility (imported, no MCL violations); recycled irrigation water under-characterized.
Hypothetical SIR scenarios show reported count exceeds expectation but rest on unverified counts and boundary/ascertainment bias - warrants investigation, not conclusion.
